transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Redwood: Alex Chen, Priya Nair | Cumulus Health: Jared Miller (CTO), Sofia Alvarez (ML Lead), Maya Patel (Security), Liam O'Connor (Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand Cumulus's evaluation of Redwood's hosted API and potential Dedicated/private options. Focus on PLG/self-serve onboarding (time-to-first-token), free credits for experimenters, and production requirements (latency, data residency, SOC2).

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, i'm alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. quick intro, my co-worker priya is our solutions engineer, she'll run through the technical bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jared Miller: good thanks, hey alex, yeah we got about 45 minutes set aside. i'm jared, cto at cumulus. we have sofia and maya on for technical and security.
[00:17] Sofia Alvarez: hi all, thanks for setting this up. excited to hear about quickstart and what the free credits look like.
[00:22] Priya Nair: great, i'll try to cover time-to-first-token, SDKs, and demo how an engineer would onboard with the PLG flow. i'll also call out differences between hosted, dedicated and private.
[00:30] [00:30] Alex Chen: quick note, if we get into infra we may switch over to priya for deep-dive, but for now goal is to map requirements and success criteria.

[02:00] Priya Nair: okay so PLG quickstart, the usual path is sign up, you get free credits to test generation and embeddings, we have quickstart templates, and a sample repo. typical time-to-first-token for an engineer who uses our SDK is around 10-15 minutes, assuming they have an API key and firewall allows outbound. sometimes with stricter network policies it takes longer.
[02:25] Maya Patel: when you say free credits, are those tied to an email domain, or to a org? and are there limits on request rates?
[02:35] Alex Chen: good q — credits are issued at org level for new sign-ups, you can allocate to users. rate limits are default but we can bump for pilots, and for Dedicated you'd get reserved capacity so different throttling.
[02:48] Liam O'Connor: our infra team is strict about egress and we host some PHI-like telem data, so we need to know about data residency and private deploy options.
[02:58] Priya Nair: absolutely. Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option for regulated workloads. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud with optional VPC peering and customer-managed keys. Hosted is fastest to onboard but data goes through Redwood's hosted endpoints unless you enable private instance.

[05:10] Sofia Alvarez: wanted to confirm, for a quick experiment we prefer hosted since it's fastest. for production we might need Dedicated or Private depending on the audit. what's the difference in latency/cost if we move from hosted to dedicated?
[05:30] Priya Nair: Dedicated gives predictable tail latency because of reserved GPU pools; cost per token might be lower at scale because of reserved capacity and better batching. Hosted varies depending on model, but it's the quickest to get started. For some customers we've seen a 10-30% cost improvement when moving to Dedicated depending on load.
[05:50] Jared Miller: do you have any hard SLO numbers we can share with ops? like p95 for small responses?
[06:00] Priya Nair: we publish performance profiles per model in the catalog. for example on the 7b-class model we see p95s in 150-300ms on Dedicated with our optimized runtime; hosted p95s depend on shared load but typically under 500-700ms for similar sizes. i'll send the benchmark sheet after.

[08:20] Maya Patel: very important for us is encryption and key management. do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? and is audit logging available?
[08:35] Alex Chen: yes, KM S integration is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit, and we provide audit logs as an add-on. we'll share the SOC2 report and architecture whitepaper.

[10:05] Sofia Alvarez: on the SDK side, what's the onboarding like for the ML team? we mostly use python and go.
[10:15] Priya Nair: we have Python and Go SDKs, plus a simple REST API. sample repo gets you to first token in ~10-15 mins: pip install, export REDWOOD_API_KEY, run sample. authentication is via API key or SSO for orgs.
[10:32] Liam O'Connor: SSO — do you support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning?
[10:38] Alex Chen: yes SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC in console. we'll share the SSO setup doc.

[12:00] Jared Miller: for our pilot, we want to spin up a team of 6 engineers and run a couple of generation and embedding workloads. what's the typical free credit allocation?
[12:15] Alex Chen: our standard PLG free credits for new orgs is enough for a few thousand token-generations and embeddings—it's designed for experimentation. for a formal pilot we can apply an expanded credit pack or trial Dedicated with reserved capacity for a short period.
[12:35] Sofia Alvarez: can we run evals and compare to our baseline? we'd like to compare latency and cost across models.
[12:42] Priya Nair: yep that's common. we'll provide a benchmark template and can run side-by-side tests. we also recommend pinning model versions and setting rollout policies during the pilot so you can measure regressions.

[15:00] [15:00] Priya Nair: quick demo snippet: signing up is self-serve, you create an org, get credits, SDK example, run a single generate call. i'm going to paste pseudo CLI logs: "export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx
python sample_gen.py --model redwood-7b" 
(brief pause) the sample repo also includes an embeddings example and a simple caching config.

[18:40] Maya Patel: i noticed in other vendors that sometimes transcription and entity masking is not guaranteed. we need clarity on retention and whether logs are retained by default.
[18:55] Alex Chen: retention defaults to 30 days for the hosted product but can be adjusted; Dedicated/private gives you more control. we can sign an agreement for no retention for certain data classes. we'll send specifics.

[21:10] Liam O'Connor: for our pilot success criteria we should define targets: latency under 500ms p95 for small prompts, cost per 1k tokens under a target, and ability to provision tokens for team members. we also need SOC2 and a security questionnaire answered.
[21:30] Alex Chen: sounds good — can you share a simple list of KPIs? we'll map them to a pilot plan.

[23:00] Sofia Alvarez: one more: model lifecycle — can we pin versions and rollback? and do you support automatic fallback to smaller models?
[23:15] Priya Nair: yes, you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and set automatic fallback policies to cheaper/smaller variants. console shows per-route usage and regressions.

[26:50] Jared Miller: question on the private deployment: if we go private on-prem, how long does it take to stand up? and what kind of support is required?
[27:05] Priya Nair: for on-prem it's typically multi-week: installation, KMS/HSM config, network tests. we have an enterprise playbook and professional services to help. for VPC-hosted private instances it's faster — usually a few days to provision once networking is approved.

[30:00] Maya Patel: are there compliance controls for data residency in EU? we have users in EU and US.
[30:10] Alex Chen: yes we have region-aware routing and can place Dedicated or Private instances in EU regions; hosted can also function from EU region endpoints. we'll document available regions.

[32:40] Priya Nair: i want to call out the quick wins: 1) Hosted for experiments (fastest to on-board, PLG credits), 2) Dedicated for predictable production throughput and lower per-token cost at scale, 3) Private for strict data residency and air-gap requirements.

[34:10] Jared Miller: ok practically speaking, how do we start the pilot? we'd like to do a 4-week pilot with 6 engineers testing generation + embeddings and run benchmarks.
[34:22] Alex Chen: proposed plan: sign up and get config + free credits for initial experiments (week 0-1), then enable an expanded pilot with reserved capacity (Dedicated trial) for weeks 2-5 to test tail latency and cost. we'll provide the benchmark template and help run it.

[36:00] Sofia Alvarez: what's your support model during pilot — Slack? email?
[36:10] Alex Chen: standard PLG support is email and community, for pilots we include SRE/SE support and a Slack channel. for Dedicated/private we offer higher-tier support with SLA.

[38:25] Maya Patel: security wise, please share SOC2, encrypt-at-rest details, KMS options, audit logs, and the questionnaire answers.
[38:35] Alex Chen: noted, we'll send SOC2, architecture whitepaper, and answers to your questionnaire.

[40:00] [40:00] Alex Chen: all right, quick recap — action items: i'll send pricing/pilot terms, priya will share benchmark template and sample prompts, maya will send the security questionnaire and we'll return answers, and liam will provide expected QPS. we'll target the pilot kickoff next week pending legal.
[40:20] Jared Miller: great thanks — looking forward to it.
[40:25] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive.
[40:35] Maya Patel: thanks all.
